concept.assembly_path: Place the lightning rotor against the cloud face with its guide pin at the closed track end, pass the rainbow's square drive through the lightning socket, and seat the drive in the cloud's round pivot pocket. No part flexes or snaps.
assumptions: A 87 x 65 x 12.8 mm object is pocket-size for this Wish; no formal pocket envelope was supplied.
A removable snug square connection is preferable to a brittle retention snap even though drop retention remains physically unverified.
Optional color may enhance the tableau, but the arch and zig remain shape-readable in one material.

components.form: A 6.0 mm thick union of five overlapping cloud volumes with two shallow closed-eye grooves, a small round mouth, a blind round pivot pocket, and a blind 90-degree guide slot.
components.interfaces: The round pocket clears the corners of P2's 5.0 mm square drive by 0.30 mm radially; the swept slot is derived from P3's 3.2 mm guide pin with 0.20 mm clearance per side and broad circular endcaps.
components.name: Sleepy cloud receiver
components.placement: Fixed at the back of the two front rotors; XY carries the cloud silhouette, +Z runs toward the rear, and the reveal pivot is at (0, 11) mm.
components.purpose: Supplies the stable cloud silhouette, sleepy face, central bearing pocket, blind guide track, and flat standing edge.

components.form: A 3.0 mm thick, 5.0 mm band semicircular arch joined to an 8.5 mm hub by a broad 7.0 mm bridge and circular root pad; rounded endcaps remove knife edges; a 5.0 mm square shaft grows vertically from the hub.
components.interfaces: The square drive passes through P3's derived 5.2 mm socket and enters P1's blind round pivot pocket; the shaft-to-socket nominal clearance is 0.10 mm per side.
components.name: Rainbow drive rotor
components.placement: Outermost front layer, 0.40 mm clear of P3; modeled in the disguised closed pose and rotated 90 degrees in the deployed assembly.
components.purpose: Provides the grasped outer control, the recognizable open rainbow, and the square shaft that drives the lightning rotor with the same turn.

components.form: A 3.0 mm thick backed zigzag made from 6.0 mm broad bars and round junctions, joined to an 8.0 mm hub with a through square socket and a 3.2 mm guide pin on a broad root.
components.interfaces: The square socket is derived once from P2's drive; the guide pin enters P1's blind swept slot and contacts its endcaps only on over-travel.
components.name: Lightning guide rotor
components.placement: Middle front layer between P1 and P2 with 0.40 mm face gaps; it shares the same pivot and angle as P2.
components.purpose: Turns the coupled motion into a second storm symbol and supplies the track follower that defines the 0- and 90-degree endpoints.

concept.intended_interaction: Hold the cloud by its side puffs, rotate the outer curved piece clockwise through one quarter-turn until the broad stop, view the rainbow and lightning as a miniature storm tableau on the cloud face, then reverse the same turn to restore the sleepy cloud outline.

print_plan.P1: Flip the product frame so the cloud's blind pockets and face grooves open upward; print flat without support.
print_plan.P2: Place its broad motif plate on the bed and grow the square shaft vertically; print without support.
print_plan.P3: Place its broad motif plate on the bed and grow the guide pin vertically; the square socket is a vertical through-cut; print without support.
print_plan.baseline_process: Deterministic target: 0.4 mm nozzle on a 220 x 220 x 220 mm bed in rigid PLA or PETG. This records digital eligibility, not a completed print.

concept.service_path: Pull the rainbow straight out of the removable snug socket and pivot pocket, lift the lightning guide pin out of its track, and separate the three pieces for cleaning or fit adjustment.
concept.signature_decision: Use two stacked motif rotors on one front-to-back axis: the outer rainbow carries an integral square drive through the inner lightning, while the lightning carries a broad guide pin in the cloud's blind quarter-circle track. The drive synchronizes both pieces and the track provides positive closed and open stops.

state_model.closed: Both motif plates are inverse-rotated into the cloud footprint; direct silhouette inspection shows no protruding lightning or rainbow geometry.
state_model.open: P2 reads as a rounded rainbow arch and P3 as a broad lightning zig on the cloud face; the guide pin is at the scene endcap.
state_model.reset: Reverse the same quarter-turn until the guide pin reaches the closed endcap and the sleepy cloud silhouette is restored.
state_model.reveal_motion: Rotate P2 clockwise 90 degrees about the common Z axis. Its square shaft rotates P3, and P3's guide pin sweeps the blind cloud track while all three plates remain separated by nominal gaps.

concept.summary: A flat three-piece sleepy-cloud puzzle whose outer curl turns 90 degrees, driving a hidden zig through a square coupling so the curl becomes a rainbow arch and the zig becomes a lightning bolt together, then reverses to a clean cloud silhouette.
concept.title: Storm Reveal
unresolved_risks: Printer-specific torque, socket friction, accidental pull-out, surface feel, wear life, and successful printing require physical evidence.
The digital hard-stop sweep establishes rigid-body blocking but not comfortable finger force or long-term guide-pin durability.
An uncoached user's recognition and delight have not been observed because Spark proceeds directly from Make to Release without Playtest.

deterministic_plan: Generate a labeled deployed assembly plus one printable entry for each of the three parts.
Audit every mating dimension from one shared parameter derivation with cadfits.
Sweep the lightning guide and rainbow drive from open to closed in 19 steps and probe four degrees beyond both endcaps for blocking.
Validate every solid and check seated assembly interference.
Export each print target to STL, then check bed contact, watertightness, manifoldness, winding, connected shells, positive volume, and 0.8 mm minimum wall for a 0.4 mm nozzle.
Inspect closed-state and part silhouettes; compare source and exact STEP in three orthogonal views.
research.evidence_limits: The Make evidence supports exact geometry, motion-envelope, print-file, and nominal-clearance claims only. It does not establish an actual print, physical fit, safe long-term wear, tactile satisfaction, or human response.

mechanism_options.interaction: One outer square drive rotates a separate rainbow and lightning rotor through a quarter-turn while a blind guide track supplies two stops.
mechanism_options.risk: Removable fit and tactile torque require physical follow-up.
mechanism_options.strength: Exactly three literal pieces, all flat-print, direct shape transformation, no hardware, no snap, and simple inspectable bores/slots.

mechanism_options.interaction: A single scene-bearing disc swaps a blank half for an upright relief behind a cloud mask.
mechanism_options.risk: A third keeper part and bayonet receiver add support-sensitive retention geometry, while rainbow and lightning cease to be separate puzzle pieces.
mechanism_options.strength: Compact and fully captured with strong masking.

mechanism_options.interaction: A twist translates a tableau outward on helical followers.
mechanism_options.risk: Long overhung tracks and stacked tolerance create binding and support risks inside a three-part limit.

mechanism_options.interaction: A twist releases shell halves around a fixed scene.
mechanism_options.risk: Requires a second pull or stored flex after the twist, contradicting the single-action request.

research.research_scope: No external factual lookup was needed. Mechanism dimensions and clearances are explicit design choices evaluated against the exact CAD and are not represented as universal printer facts or physical observations.
